title: Acquired × 张忠谋 — 接下苹果，只接一半
title_en: Acquired × Morris Chang — Take Apple, but only half

questions.question: 按张忠谋在访谈里给出的裁员规则，哪种情况下不该裁员？
options: 遣散费低于这批人一整年的薪水，因为这时裁员在账面上就是一笔实打实的净省钱
公司已经连续两个季度营收下滑，因为这说明需求再也回不来了
预计一年内需求回升、还得把人招回来，因为遣散约半年薪水加培训至少半年
被裁对象是考评最差的一批人，因为绩效差的人留下来只会拖累团队
questions.explanation: 张忠谋的账是：遣散通常要付半年左右薪水，培养一个人又至少半年，一年内要招回就两头亏。他还反对按绩效裁人，因为七百个差评出自七百个主管，本身就主观；半导体有摩尔定律撑着，需求总会回来。
questions.question_en: By the layoff rule Morris Chang lays out in the interview, when should a company not lay people off?
options_en: When severance costs less than a full year of their salaries, because then the layoff saves money on paper
When revenue has fallen for two straight quarters, because that shows the demand is never coming back
When demand should recover within a year and you'd rehire, since severance is about six months' pay and training takes at least six
When the people cut are the lowest-rated performers, because keeping weak performers only drags the team down
questions.explanation_en: Chang's arithmetic: severance usually runs about half a year's pay and training a replacement takes at least half a year, so rehiring within a year loses on both ends. He also opposed performance-based cuts because 700 bad ratings come from 700 subjective supervisors, and in semiconductors Moore's law means demand returns.

questions.question: 台积电面对苹果 20 纳米订单时只接了需求的一半。节目对这个「一半」的分析是什么？
options: 台积电当时筹不到足够的资金扩产，又不愿发债或增发新股，只能先接一半
学习曲线主张吃下全部产量，但全接等于拿公司存亡去赌一个客户的销量预测，一半是两者的折中
苹果开出的 40% 毛利率低于台积电的 45%，接一半是为了守住整体毛利率
为了保住股息，台积电只能把资本支出砍半，订单也就只能接下一半
questions.explanation: 按学习曲线，产量越大成本降得越快，应该整单吃下；可苹果的预测差个百分之五到十，整个节点的利润就没了。钱其实是靠发公司债筹的，股息也没砍；毛利率之争张忠谋当时没接话，问题核心在节点取舍和风险。
questions.question_en: Facing Apple's 20 nm order, TSMC took only half the requested volume. How does the episode explain that "half"?
options_en: TSMC couldn't raise enough money to expand and refused to issue bonds or new shares, so it could only take half
The learning curve says take all the volume, but taking it all bets the company on one customer's forecast; half splits the difference
Apple's offered 40% gross margin was below TSMC's 45%, so taking half protected the company's overall margin
To keep paying its dividend, TSMC had to halve capital spending, which meant taking only half the order
questions.explanation_en: By the learning curve, more volume drives cost down faster, so you'd take the whole order; but if Apple's forecast missed by 5–10%, the node's entire profit would vanish. The money was in fact raised through corporate bonds and the dividend was kept; Chang let the margin remark pass, and the real issue was node risk.

questions.question: Tim Cook 对张忠谋说「英特尔根本不懂怎么做代工」。张忠谋自己怎么理解这句话？
options: 说的是制程：英特尔的工艺当时已经落后台积电好几代，造不出苹果要的芯片
说的是服务：客户的要求有的近乎荒唐，台积电学会了每一个都客气回应，英特尔从不这样
说的是价格：英特尔的代工报价远高于台积电，苹果算下来无法接受这笔成本
说的是利益冲突：英特尔自己也设计芯片，会和代工客户抢生意，客户因此不敢下单
questions.explanation: 主持人把这句话解读为利益冲突，张忠谋当场表示不同意：他认为 Cook 说的是服务与信任，并举例说他认识的台湾 PC 厂商没有一个喜欢英特尔。代工的核心能力在于怎样对待客户，而不只是会不会和客户竞争。
questions.question_en: Tim Cook told Morris Chang that "Intel doesn't know how to be a foundry." How did Chang himself interpret the remark?
options_en: As about process technology: Intel's manufacturing was already generations behind TSMC and couldn't make Apple's chips
As about service: some customer requests are nearly absurd, TSMC learned to answer each one courteously, and Intel never did
As about price: Intel's foundry quotes were far above TSMC's, and Apple found the cost unacceptable
As about conflict of interest: Intel designs its own chips and would compete with foundry customers, so they won't order
questions.explanation_en: The hosts read the remark as conflict of interest, and Chang disagreed on the spot: he took Cook to mean service and trust, noting that none of the Taiwanese PC makers he knew liked Intel. A foundry's core skill is how it treats customers, not merely whether it competes with them.
